entries.gloss: Moses' brother, first high priest of Israel.
Second son of Adam and Eve, slain by his brother Cain.
Father of the faithful; God made covenant with him.
The first man, formed from the dust.
King of Israel who followed Baal with Jezebel.
Shepherd-prophet who cried for justice in Israel.
Fisherman, first called; he brought Peter to Jesus.
Messenger of God, ministering to the heirs of salvation.
Aged prophetess who recognized the infant Jesus in the temple.
To set apart with oil for office or burial.
Eloquent Alexandrian preacher of the Scriptures.
One sent by Christ to witness and found the church.
Tentmaker with Priscilla; fellow worker of Paul.
Mountains where the ark came to rest.
Gold-covered chest bearing the tablets and the mercy seat.
Field of the last battle in Revelation.
King of Judah who began by seeking the LORD.
Chief musician of David; many psalms bear his name.
Covering of sin by sacrifice; reconciliation with God.
Companion of Daniel, also called Abednego.
Great city of exile; image of proud empire.
Washing with water into repentance and new life.
Son of encouragement; Paul's companion on the first journey.
Scribe of Jeremiah; his book is in the canon.
Wife of Uriah, then of David; mother of Solomon.
Well of the oath; southern bound of the land.
King of Babylon who saw the writing on the wall.
Youngest son of Jacob; father of a tribe of Israel.
Village near Jerusalem, home of Lazarus, Mary, and Martha.
House of God; where Jacob dreamed of the ladder.
City of David; birthplace of Jesus.
God's spoken favour, given and passed down.
Life poured out; price of covenant and atonement.
Kinsman-redeemer who married Ruth.
Whole sacrifice ascending in smoke to the LORD.
High priest who presided over Jesus' trial.
Firstborn of Adam and Eve; slew his brother Abel.
Faithful spy who entered the promised land with Joshua.
Land promised to Abraham and his seed.
Town on the Sea of Galilee; base of Jesus' ministry.
Winged guardians of the throne and the ark.
Sign of the covenant in Abraham's flesh.
God's spoken law; ten words on Sinai.
Port city where Paul planted a church.
Centurion whose household first received the Gentile gospel.
Binding promise of God with his people.
God's making of heaven and earth from nothing.
Roman instrument of shame, become the sign of salvation.
Royal honour; also the victor's wreath of life.
Judgment pronounced on disobedience.
King of Persia who let the exiles return and rebuild.
City on the road where Saul met the risen Christ.
Exile in Babylon, interpreter of dreams, servant of God.
Absence of light; image of sin and judgment.
Shepherd, psalmist, and king after God's own heart.
God's appointed day of judgment and deliverance.
Wages of sin; enemy destroyed by resurrection.
Prophetess and judge who led Israel to victory.
Philistine woman who betrayed Samson for silver.
Accuser and tempter; adversary of God's people.
Learner who follows Jesus and keeps his words.
Night vision by which God warned and guided.
Garden of God's planting, home of the first man and woman.
Land of bondage and of refuge; Israel's exodus began there.
Priest of Shiloh who raised the boy Samuel.
Prophet of fire who was taken up in a whirlwind.
Elijah's successor; prophet of miracles in Israel.
Mother of John the Baptist; kinswoman of Mary.
Village where the risen Jesus broke bread with two disciples.
Seventh from Adam; he walked with God and was taken.
Great city of Asia; home of a church Paul loved.
Son of Joseph; his name for the northern kingdom.
Eldest son of Isaac, who sold his birthright.
Jewish queen of Persia who saved her people.
Life of the age to come, known in Christ now.
Land of the south; its church keeps the full canon.
The first woman, mother of all living.
Exile-prophet of visions, the valley of bones, the temple.
Scribe who brought the law back to Jerusalem.
Trust in God and his promises, counted as righteousness.
Abstaining from food in repentance and seeking God.
God's presence, judgment, and refining.
First and best, given to God as pledge of the harvest.
Release from debt of sin, given and commanded.
Angel who announced births to Daniel, Zechariah, and Mary.
Nations outside Israel, grafted in by faith.
Garden where Jesus prayed before his arrest.
Judge who defeated Midian with three hundred men.
Hill country east of Jordan, famed for its balm.
First camp in the land; stones of remembrance.
Weight of God's presence and honour.
Place of the skull; hill of the crucifixion.
Philistine giant felled by David's sling.
Land in Egypt settled by Jacob's family.
Good news of Jesus Christ, crucified and risen.
Unmerited favour of God in Christ.
Prophet who asked why the wicked prosper.
Handmaid of Sarah; mother of Ishmael.
Prophet who urged the returned exiles to rebuild the temple.
Praise the LORD.
Mother of Samuel; her prayer became a song.
City where Abraham stayed on the way to Canaan.
God's dwelling; the skies above; the age to come.
Ancient city; burial place of the patriarchs.
Place of final judgment for the wicked.
King of Judea at Jesus' birth; his house opposed the gospel.
King of Judah whose prayer turned back Assyria.
Third person of the Trinity; giver of life and gifts.
Save now; the crowd's cry at the entry into Jerusalem.
Prophet whose marriage pictured God's faithful love.
Image of false gods, forbidden by the law.
Fragrant offering rising like prayer.
Portion given by God to his children.
Son of promise, bound on the altar, father of Jacob.
Prophet of the suffering servant and the new heavens.
Son of Abraham and Hagar; father of a great nation.
Son of Isaac, renamed Israel; father of the twelve tribes.
Apostle, son of Zebedee, martyred by Herod; also James brother of the Lord.
Weeping prophet of Jerusalem's fall and the new covenant.
Walled city that fell at the trumpet blast.
First king of the divided northern kingdom.
Holy city; place of the temple and the cross.
Father of David; the shoot from his stump is Messiah.
The Christ, Son of God, crucified and risen.
Priest of Midian, father-in-law and counsellor of Moses.
Queen who promoted Baal and hunted Elijah.
David's commander, mighty and ruthless.
Righteous sufferer who held fast and saw God.
Prophet of the locusts and the outpoured Spirit.
Forerunner who baptized in the Jordan and prepared the way.
Reluctant prophet swallowed by a great fish, sent to Nineveh.
Son of Saul; David's truest friend.
River of crossing: Joshua, Elijah, and Jesus' baptism.
Dreamer sold into Egypt, who saved his family; also the name of Mary's husband, guardian of Jesus.
Moses' successor who led Israel into the land.
Boy king who restored the law and the Passover.
Fiftieth year of release, return, and rest.
Fourth son of Jacob; his tribe bore the kings, and his name the southern kingdom.
Apostle who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
Brother of James; his letter warns against false teachers.
God's righteous verdict on the living and the dead.
Widow whose courage delivered Bethulia from Holofernes.
God's reign, present in Christ and coming in fullness.
Passover sacrifice; Christ, the Lamb of God.
Two men bear the name: Lamech of Cain's line, and Lamech father of Noah.
Torah; God's instruction given through Moses.
Friend of Jesus, raised from the tomb at Bethany.
First wife of Jacob; mother of six tribes.
Yeast; image of small corrupting influence.
Mountains of cedar for temple and palace.
Son of Jacob; father of the priestly tribe.
Great sea creature; image of chaos tamed by God.
God's first word; Christ the light of the world.
Abraham's nephew, rescued from Sodom.
Beloved physician; author of the Gospel and Acts.
Seller of purple; first convert in Philippi.
Last prophet of the Old Testament canon.
King of Judah; his prayer of repentance is in the canon.
Bread from heaven in the wilderness.
Covenant union of man and woman, image of Christ and church.
Sister of Lazarus and Mary; she served and confessed Christ.
Virgin of Nazareth, mother of the Lord; the name also of Magdalene, of Bethany, and others.
First witness of the risen Jesus.
Tax collector called to be apostle and evangelist.
Chosen by lot to replace Judas among the Twelve.
King of Salem and priest of God Most High.
God's compassion withholding deserved judgment.
Anointed one; the Christ.
Prophet who asked what the LORD requires: justice, mercy, humility.
Archangel who contends for God's people.
Desert land of Moses' exile and Gideon's victory.
Sign of God's power breaking into the world.
Sister of Moses; prophetess who sang at the sea.
Land east of the Dead Sea; home of Ruth.
Cousin and guardian of Esther at the Persian court.
Lawgiver who led Israel out of Egypt to Sinai.
Burial spice; gift of the wise men.
Prophet who foretold the fall of Nineveh.
Mother-in-law of Ruth; from bitterness to blessing.
Prophet who confronted David over Bathsheba.
Town where Jesus grew up.
King of Babylon who carried Judah into exile.
Cupbearer who rebuilt Jerusalem's walls.
Pharisee who came to Jesus by night.
Great Assyrian city that repented at Jonah's preaching.
Righteous man who built the ark and survived the flood.
Sworn promise calling God as witness.
Prophet whose single chapter judges Edom.
Gift brought to God on the altar.
Garden of delight; the blessed place of the dead.
Feast of Israel's deliverance from Egypt.
Endurance under trial, fruit of the Spirit.
Island of John's exile and the Revelation.
Apostle to the Gentiles, once Saul the persecutor.
Wholeness with God; the gift of the risen Christ.
Feast of weeks; day the Spirit fell on the church.
Fisherman called the rock; first among the apostles.
Party of the law, zealous for tradition.
Apostle and evangelist; baptized the Ethiopian eunuch.
Roman colony; first church in Europe.
Roman governor who sentenced Jesus to the cross.
Blow of judgment, as on Egypt.
Speaking and listening before God.
Mediator who offers sacrifice and blessing.
Tentmaker with Aquila; teacher of Apollos.
God's word spoken through his prophets.
One called to speak God's word to his people.
Short saying of wisdom for daily life.
Sacred song of praise, lament, and trust.
Beloved wife of Jacob; mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
Woman of Jericho who hid the spies and joined Israel.
Sign of God's covenant with Noah after the flood.
Wife of Isaac; mother of Jacob and Esau.
Waters parted for Israel's escape from Egypt.
Son of Solomon, under whom the kingdom divided.
Turning from sin to God.
Rising from death to new life; Christ's and ours.
Right standing with God, gift and calling.
Capital of empire; Paul's destination and martyrdom.
Moabite widow whose loyalty brought her to Bethlehem.
Seventh day of rest, holy to the LORD.
Offering of life to God for sin and thanks.
Party of priests who denied resurrection.
Deliverance from sin and death by God.
Capital of the north; its people heard the gospel.
Judge of great strength, undone by Delilah.
Last judge and prophet who anointed Saul and David.
Holy place of God's dwelling among his people.
Wife of Abraham; mother of Isaac in her old age.
Adversary; accuser of the brethren.
First king of Israel, rejected for disobedience; also the birth name of Paul.
Teacher and copyist of the law.
Writings breathed out by God.
Burning ones who cry Holy around the throne.
Tempter in Eden; image of the devil.
City of covenant, between Gerizim and Ebal.
Guardian of the flock; the LORD and his Christ.
First home of the tabernacle in the land.
Missing the mark; rebellion against God.
Mountain of the law and the covenant.
City judged by fire; Lot escaped it.
Son of David; king of wisdom who built the temple.
Life and person of man, made in God's image.
Breath and power of God.
Light of heaven; sign of promise and of kings.
First martyr; deacon full of faith and the Spirit.
Tent of meeting in the wilderness.
Cilician city; birthplace of Paul.
House of God in Jerusalem.
Trial to sin; Christ overcame it for us.
Macedonian city of Paul's second journey.
Apostle who doubted until he touched the risen Lord.
Paul's true son in the faith; pastor at Ephesus.
Tenth given to God and his servants.
Paul's fellow worker; pastor in Crete.
Son of Tobit, guided by Raphael to healing and marriage.
Righteous exile whose story is told in Tobit.
Languages given by the Spirit at Pentecost.
Christ revealed in glory on the mountain.
Tree in Eden and in the new Jerusalem.
Distress of the last days and of the faithful.
Horn of assembly, war, and the last day.
Faithfulness of God; Christ himself.
Phoenician port, proud and judged.
State barred from the holy until cleansed.
Chaldean city; Abraham's first home.
Curtain before the holy of holies, torn at the cross.
Israel and Christ, source of fruit.
Young woman; Mary, mother of Jesus.
Sight given by God to prophets and seers.
Angels who descended in Enoch's account.
Skill for living in God's fear; Christ our wisdom.
One who testifies to what he has seen.
God's righteous anger against sin.
Priest, father of John the Baptist; prophet of the restoration.
Prophet of the day of the LORD in Josiah's reign.
Hill of Jerusalem; name for God's holy city.

note: Refs follow the Standard text; versification is identical in the Modern edition.
